goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group editor template wrapped in <form class="form-horizontal"> with no submit prevention; pressing Enter in the group-name input triggers native form submission causing a full page reload that discards unsaved edits

adjudication.rationale: The diff wraps the group editor in a raw `<form class="form-horizontal">` (admin/templates/group.hbs) but does not attach any Ember `{{action ... on="submit"}}` handler to the form to prevent default submission. The name field (`{{text-field ...}}`) is inside this form, and the save `<button>` has no explicit `type`, so it is a submit button by default. While Ember’s `{{action "save"}}` on the button will prevent default on click, pressing Enter in the text field triggers the form’s native `submit` event (not a button click), which would cause a normal browser form submission/navigation (full page reload) and can discard unsaved edits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No failure handlers on AJAX calls in addMembers/removeMember; server failures like 422 are silently ignored with no message or state update

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `addMembers`/`removeMember` call `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` without any `.catch`/error callback, so there is no *local* failure handling added here. However, the finding’s stronger claim that failures (e.g., 422) are “silently ignored with no message or state update” is not verifiable from the diff alone because `Discourse.ajax` may provide centralized/global error handling elsewhere (not shown), and many other existing AJAX usages follow the same pattern. Thus it’s a reasonable UX concern, but not a clearly demonstrable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: usernames input is never cleared after a successful add, allowing re-submission of the same list and stale UI contents after members reload

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` and contains an explicit `// TODO: should clear the input`, but there is no subsequent `this.set("usernames", null/"")` (nor does `Group.addMembers` clear it). Since the `user-selector` component is bound to `usernames` (`{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}`), the input will retain the previously submitted list even after the members list reloads via `findMembers()`, enabling an easy re-submit of the same stale value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: limit and offset params in groups_controller.rb members action have no bounds validation; limit=9999999 dumps entire membership and negative values are passed into ActiveRecord with undefined behavior

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members` the diff introduces pagination params `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then uses them directly in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no clamping/validation. A caller can supply an extremely large `limit` to force a very large query/response, and can supply negative values (e.g., `limit=-1` or `offset=-10`) which are not prevented here and may raise errors or behave unexpectedly depending on ActiveRecord/RDBMS. This is directly verifiable from the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking API change without deprecation: GET admin/groups/:id/users removed, PATCH update flow dropped, and create/update no longer accept usernames, breaking existing API consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes/changes several previously-supported admin group endpoints and request shapes without keeping backward-compatible handlers. In `config/routes.rb`, the `get "users"` route under `admin/groups` is removed and replaced with `put "members"` and `delete "members"`, so any client calling the old `.../admin/groups/:id/users` (or similar) will fail. In `Admin::GroupsController`, the PATCH-based incremental membership update flow (`update_patch` and branching on `request.patch?`) is deleted; `update` now only supports direct params and no longer processes `params[:changes]`. Also `create`/`update` stop accepting `params[:group][:usernames]` / `params[:group]` payloads and instead expect top-level `name/visible/alias_level`, with membership changes moved to new `add_members`/`remove_member` actions. These are concrete, verifiable breaking API changes that would break existing API consumers expecting the old endpoints/payloads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips usernames that don't match any user and returns success even if zero members were added, giving no indication of typo'd names

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds a user if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record; non-existent usernames are simply ignored. After the loop it calls `group.save` and renders `success_json` on success, with no check that any members were actually added. Therefore, a typo or all-invalid usernames will still return 200 success with no indication that nothing happened.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member doesn't check that user_id is actually a member of the group; removing a non-member returns success, masking no-op operations

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. If `user_id` is not currently in the group, `delete` is a no-op and the request will still return success. However, this behavior is consistent with an idempotent “remove” API and nothing in the diff indicates the endpoint is intended to error when the user is not a member. Therefore the finding asserts a problem based on an implied requirement that is not present in the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests for the new public groups#members pagination behavior (limit/offset clamping, meta shape) or the JS pagination logic consuming it

adjudication.rationale: The diff materially changes the public `GroupsController#members` response from `render_serialized(members, GroupUserSerializer)` to a new JSON shape `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` and adds pagination params (`limit`, `offset`) without adding any corresponding tests for this endpoint or for edge cases like limit/offset handling. The only specs touched are `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` (admin controller), and there are no new specs for `GroupsController` or for the Ember pagination behavior (`currentPage`, `totalPages`, next/previous actions) consuming `meta`. So the claim that there are no tests for the new pagination/meta behavior is directly verifiable in the diff.
